pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 15.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: POEMS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.4: Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why is it important to relate ideas read in works of art to real life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. explain why it is important to relate ideas learnt in poems to real life
2. identify the key elements of an email
3. apply the elements in writing an email
4. appreciate the importance of writing emails

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems

Teach
• Focus skill: explain why it is important to relate ideas learnt in poems to real life.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to relate ideas read in works of art to real life?
2. What is the role of poems in the society?
3. Why do we write emails?
4. What is the difference between emails and letters?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
